record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a polycyclic group and let Aut(G) be its automorphism group. Given automorphisms of G, determine the computational complexity of the conjugacy problem in Aut(G), that is, the problem of deciding whether the automorphisms are conjugate inside the automorphism group.

evidence.quote: For groups G in the larger class of polycyclic-by-finite (or virtually polycyclic) groups, the conjugacy decision problem is decidable in Aut(G) [38].
(7) What is the complexity of the conjugacy problem in the automorphism of polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a finite subnormal series $G = G_0 \triangleright G_1 \triangleright \cdots \triangleright G_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Such a group is finitely presented, and its automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ is known to be finitely presentable. The conjugacy problem in $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ asks, given two automorphisms $\varphi,\psi \in \operatorname{Aut}(G)$ (specified by their images on a fixed finite generating set of $G$), to decide whether there exists $\theta \in \operatorname{Aut}(G)$ such that $\psi = \theta\varphi\theta^{-1}$. It is known that this problem is decidable when $G$ is polycyclic (and more generally polycyclic-by-finite). Determine the computational complexity of the conjugacy problem in $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ as $G$ ranges over polycyclic groups: provide tight upper and lower bounds (e.g., polynomial-time, NP, PSPACE, EXPTIME, or hardness in some such class) for the decision problem, in both the non-uniform setting (fixed $G$) and the uniform setting (where $G$ is part of the input).
artifact.category_tag: Algorithmic group theory / conjugacy in Aut(G)
artifact.status_search_result: Decidability of the conjugacy problem in Aut(G) for polycyclic (and polycyclic-by-finite) G is known, but the precise computational complexity remains open. Related work shows the uniform conjugacy problem within certain polycyclic groups themselves can be NP-complete, yet no tight complexity bounds for conjugacy inside Aut(G) of polycyclic groups appear in the literature.

status_evidence.title: A family of polycyclic groups over which the uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs polycyclic groups whose uniform conjugacy problem is NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Related complexity results exist for conjugacy in polycyclic groups, but not for Aut(G).

status_evidence.title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory (Baumslag et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open algorithmic problems concerning polycyclic groups and their automorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of conjugacy in Aut(polycyclic) is listed among open algorithmic problems.
